channel.title: mint - news
channel.description: Get the latest news and analysis on business, finance, politics from mint, the website of the Mint newspaper, one of India's leading business and financial dailies

item.title: 63% of Americans say Trump and family inappropriately benefited from ​cryptocurrency, poll finds
item.description: The survey also found that 69% of Americans believe Trump's private business interests influence his decisions as president.

item.title: Apple, Google News ‘favor Democrats’. Never endorsed a Republican presidential candidate. New study reveals
item.description: The study argues that the pattern raises questions about the political diversity of news sources promoted by major digital news aggregators.

item.title: US college applications from international students fall 10% amid Trump visa crackdown: Report
item.description: International student applications to US colleges fell about 10% this year, the biggest decline in at least a decade, as the Trump administration tightened visa rules. Applications from Asia and Africa dropped sharply, while domestic applications rose 4%.

item.title: Harry and Meghan’s $14.7M Montecito Mansion could be put up for sale — Here’s why
item.description: The couple purchased the estate for $14.65 million in 2020, shortly after stepping back from royal duties and moving to the United States.

item.title: US imposes fresh sanctions on Hezbollah, citing group's links to Iran government
item.description: As part of the new measures, Washington re-designated Hezbollah under a terrorism-related authority

item.title: Jharkhand student leaders accuse Hemant Soren govt of 'deceit' after HC stays JPSC appointment cancellations
item.description: Student leaders protesting Jharkhand recruitment exam irregularities accused the Hemant Soren government of deceit after the high court stayed its order cancelling 11th and 13th JPSC appointments. They alleged the govt failed to defend its case properly.

item.title: India allows tax-free sugar import in rare move to cool prices
item.description: India, the world’s second-biggest sugar producer, has allowed mills and refiners to import duty-free raw sugar in an effort to tame record local prices.

item.title: Iran condemns Trump's new sanctions, calls them ‘economic terrorism,’ ‘crimes against humanity’
item.description: Trump warned of sweeping economic consequences for any country that provided what he called “any type of lifeline to Iran”

item.title: IndiGo soars to record 67.4% share as India’s air traffic loses altitude
item.description: Airlines carried around 12 million passengers in July, down 5% from a year earlier and 11% from June, when traffic stood at 13.5 million. The sequential decline followed a more than 12% year-on-year drop in June, pointing to a sustained slowdown in domestic air travel demand.

item.title: Bessent warns allies, China as Trump plans ‘economic D-Day’ against Iran: ‘You are either with us or against us’
item.description: The escalation comes as President Donald Trump seeks to increase economic pressure on Tehran after months of military strikes and a US blockade that have disrupted Iranian oil exports.

item.title: Indian Oil signs five-year deal to supply petroleum products to Mauritius
item.description: The state-run refiner will meet Mauritius's petroleum needs for five years under a new bilateral agreement, reinforcing India’s role as a key regional energy exporter amid West Asia supply disruptions.

item.title: Eric Swalwell sexual assault probe: FBI raids former Congressman’s DC home, seizes electronic devices
item.description: The developments come months after Swalwell resigned from Congress following reports detailing allegations of sexual misconduct and withdrew from the race for governor of California.

item.title: 'Beyond jurisdiction': Punjab and Haryana HC sets aside Chandigarh Police promotion rules for Head Constables
item.description: The Punjab and Haryana HC has set aside Chandigarh Police's 2021 promotion rules for Head Constables, ruling the amendment was beyond the Secretary, Home Department's jurisdiction and the required procedure under the 2007 Act was not followed.

item.title: Global Fintech Fest likely to draw 500 global investors this year
item.description: Organizers expect 500 investors and over 100,000 attendees, with GFF 2026 focusing on responsible AI deployment, while new initiatives include the TokenNext platform for emerging financial infrastructure

item.title: ‘Trump’s best friends are his fan club’: Natalie Harp’s brother on her bond with President
item.description: Natalie Harp, a close aide to US President Donald Trump, has faced growing scrutiny over her unusually close proximity to the President.

item.title: BNP's Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir elected Bangladesh President in first contested poll in 35 years
item.description: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was elected Bangladesh's President after defeating Oli Ahmed 255-88 in the country's first contested presidential poll since 1991. The BNP leader will take oath on Friday as the 23rd President.

item.title: Ladakh to get J&K High Court bench: Amit Shah says move will improve access to justice in remote areas
item.description: Union Home Minister Amit Shah said the government is fully committed to the all-round development of Ladakh and to ensuring constitutional safeguards.

item.title: Delhi gets its fourth Master Plan, aims for 4 mn new houses by 2047
item.description: Delhi's new Master Plan aims to alleviate urban congestion and improve infrastructure, while also promoting redevelopment and better use of existing areas, according to city officials.

item.title: Army veterans react to viral video showing Gen Z woman’s outburst in Ladakh, ‘Before asking for entitlement…’
item.description: Retired Army veterans have criticised a woman's viral video response to checkpoint treatment in Ladakh. They highlighted the importance of understanding the soldier's sacrifices, urging her to reflect on her behaviour.

item.title: Trump’s economic threat to Iran: What it means, likely impact, what Iran and China said
item.description: However, Trump did not specify exactly what new measures Washington would impose or which countries would be targeted.

item.title: What is Clarity Act? Why Trump's push for crypto rules matters and how it is impacting Bitcoin prices
item.description: US President Donald Trump has urged Congress to pass the Clarity Act to establish clearer crypto rules. The bill remains stalled in the Senate over ethics provisions. Trump's push boosted Bitcoin above $70,000, while crypto-linked stocks also surged.

item.title: Jharkhand High Court stays Hemant Soren-led govt's order to scrap JPSC exams; 450 candidates get relief
item.description: The high court passed the interim order while hearing several petitions filed by the newly appointed candidates against the Jharkhand government's decision. The court has directed the state government to submit its response by 15 September.

item.title: CJP protests: SC sets up 5-member panel to probe police ‘excesses’ - Who is on it, what will it examine?
item.description: The court was hearing a batch of petitions alleging excessive police action against students who participated in protests at Jantar Mantar and other locations across the country over alleged NEET examination paper leaks and broader concerns relating to the examination system.

item.title: India’s reservoir storage deficit narrows, but water stress persists
item.description: A revival in monsoon rainfall has replenished reservoirs in recent weeks, but storage remains below last year’s levels across most regions, keeping pressure on irrigation, rabi sowing and hydropower generation.

item.title: WhatsApp confession, 3 bodies — Chilling details emerge in Lucknow bankers' murder-suicide case
item.description: After killing Divya, Manas uploaded a confessional WhatsApp story about his wife's murder and revealed that he was going to kill his sister and himself next, according to an HT report.

item.title: No more imports of big cats and great apes: Inside Vantara's voluntary CITES pledge to protect wildlife
item.description: Vantara said it would place greater emphasis on in situ conservation, which involves protecting and conserving wildlife in their natural habitats.

item.title: Prince Harry, Meghan Markle packing bags to return to UK with kids: Social media reacts, ‘They’re broke’
item.description: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle are planning to relocate to a private home outside London. Their children will start British schooling in September.&nbsp;

item.title: Meet Mirza Islam Alamgir and Colonel Oli Ahmed, nominees for Bangladesh presidential election
item.description: Bangladesh's presidential election commenced, marking the first contested race in 35 years. Lawmakers are voting for the 23rd president, with BNP's Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and LDP's Colonel (retd) Oli Ahmed as candidates. Results are expected shortly after the vote counting concludes.

item.title: Supreme Court upholds its landmark 1978 Bangalore Water Supply judgment about definition of ‘industry’
item.description: The Supreme Court upheld its 1978 Bangalore Water Supply judgment, confirming that future disputes will fall under the Industrial Relations Code, 2020.&nbsp;

item.title: Sajjan Kumar, serving life sentence in 1984 anti-Sikh riots, dies at 84
item.description: Sajjan Kumar was serving life sentence by the Delhi High Court in a case related to the killing of five Sikhs and the burning of a gurdwara during the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.

item.title: 'Only Indians, Americans': Pak MP claims UAE hotel denied rooms to Pakistanis after flight cancellation
item.description: Pakistani MP and former National Assembly speaker Asad Qaiser has alleged that Pakistani passengers were denied hotel accommodation in the UAE after a flight cancellation, while Indian and US passport holders were allegedly offered rooms.

item.title: Quote of the day by William Arthur Ward, ‘Judge each day not by the harvest you reap but by the seeds you plant'
item.description: Motivational writer William Arthur Ward urged people to measure their days not by immediate results but by the effort and preparation they invest. His agricultural metaphor reminds us that true progress lies in sowing seeds — of kindness, learning or opportunity — that may bear fruit later.

item.title: SC keeps labour protection intact in pending cases, leaves ‘industry’ definition under new code open
item.description: The Supreme Court has preserved existing labour protections in pending disputes. The 5:4 Constitution Bench ruling keeps the 1978 Triple Test applicable to cases still governed by the repealed Industrial Disputes Act.

item.title: From Patna to Mexico's Colima Street — How this IIT Delhi alum built 4 thriving business ventures overseas
item.description: Vijeet Suman, an IIT Delhi alumnus from Patna, established four successful ventures abroad. His entrepreneurial journey began in Mexico with a food business and expanded diverse fields.

item.title: Who is Rhiya Ahir? All about the model, FIR against her and how she hogged limelight amid Mumbai Gen Z protest?
item.description: Model Rhiya Ahir, who shot to fame after standing before a police van during Mumbai's Gen Z protest, has appealed to police to withdraw an FIR against her and take action against those allegedly threatening her online.
